title: High-throughput genetic screening of meiotic commitment using fluorescence microscopy in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
protocol: Inoculate a 20 mL culture of YPD with a colony of your yeast strain of interest and let grow for 12 h at 30°C with agitation.
Dilute 2.5 × 10^8 cells in 50 mL of pre-warmed YPD.
Incubate cells at 30°C for 4 h with constant agitation.
Boil the salmon sperm DNA for 5 min and then put on ice.
Prepare 35 μL of the transformation mix for each well, add 15 μL of 1 M Lithium acetate and 20 μL of the boiled salmon sperm DNA.
Keep this mix on ice until use.
Transfer 200 μL of the cell suspension into each well of a 96-well round bottom plate.
Centrifuge the 96-well plate at 1,300 g for 10 min.
Aspirate the supernatant using a multi-channel pipette.
Add 5 μL of miniprep DNA from the Yeast Genomic Tiling Collection to each well (100–400 ng per μL).
Add 35 μL of the transformation mix (15 μL of 1 M Lithium acetate + 20 μL of 2 mg/mL salmon sperm DNA) to each well.
Add 100 μL of 50% PEG to each well using a multi-channel pipette.
Cover the 96-well plate and shake for 10 min at 75 rpm.
Incubate at 42°C for 2 h.
Centrifuge the plate at 1,300 g for 10 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 μL of sterile water by slowly pipetting up and down.
Spot 5 μL of cells on SCD-leu plates.
Incubate the plates at 30°C for 2–4 days.
Add 1 mL of SCD-leu to each well of a sterile 96-well block.
Scrape the cells from a single spot on the SCD-leu plates and swirl into the appropriate well of the 96-well block.
Cover the block with an air permeable seal.
Incubate the 96-well block at 30°C for 24 h.
Add a 2 mm × 5 mm sterile magnetic stir bar to each well of a sterile 96-well block.
Alternatively, use glass beads instead of magnetic stir bars.
Add 1 mL of SCA-leu to each well in the block.
Transfer 40 μL of SCD-leu grown cells into each well of the 96-well block.
Cover the block with a sterile air permeable cover.
Incubate the block at 30°C for 15 h on a shaker set at 200 RPM.
Alternatively, use a stir plate to agitate the cells for proper aeration.
Tape the blocks onto a shaker.
Spin the 96-well block at 1,300 g for 1 min.
Aspirate the supernatant using a multi-channel pipette.
Wash the cells twice with 1 mL of sterile water.
Add 1 mL of sterile water to the cells.
Spin down the cells after each wash.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of SPM by pipetting up and down.
Seal the block with a sterile air permeable cover.
Incubate the cells at 25°C on a shaker set at 200 RPM until reaching the desired meiotic stage.
Spin the 96-well block at 1,300 g for 1 min when studying meiotic commitment or return-to-growth.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in 1 mL of 2×SCD -leu media.
Place the block on a magnetic stir plate at 25°C and stir at low speed for 8 hours if studying meiotic commitment or return-to-growth.
Alternatively, place plates on a shaker at low speed.
Centrifuge the block at 1,300 g for 1 min when resuspending cells in media after meiotic studies.
Aspirate the supernatant and remove 950 μL of media.
Resuspend the cells in the remaining 50 μL of media.
Transfer the cells to a 96-well round bottom plate.
Add 150 μL of freshly prepared 4% paraformaldehyde to fix the cells.
Centrifuge the 96-well plate at 1,300 g for 1 min.
Discard the paraformaldehyde and resuspend the cells in 150 μL of sterile PBS.
Centrifuge the plate at 1,300 g for 1 min.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 150 μL of sterile PBS.
Heat 1.2% agarose in 1× PBS (pH 7.4) in the microwave until dissolved.
Add 150 μL of molten agarose into each well of a clean flat-bottom 96-well plate.
Invert and place the solidified agar pad plate over the 96-well plate with cells.
Centrifuge the plates at 100 g for 1 minute to transfer the agarose pad from the top plate to the wells containing the cells.
Image cells on a fluorescence microscope.
Scan through each well and select at least 10 fields per well for imaging.
Identify fields where cells form a monolayer and are on the same focal plane using brightfield or DIC.
Image using appropriate excitation wavelengths for fluorescent tags within strains.
Take at least five z-steps (1.2 μm) for each wavelength.
Include a brightfield or DIC image.
Optimize exposure time for your imaging system and tagged proteins of interest.
Use an inverted fluorescence microscope with a 60× oil objective for imaging cells at the bottom of glass-bottom 96-well plates.
Identify 10 fields within each well to image with 5 z-stacks for both mCherry and GFP.
Analyze acquired images using software compatible with the images taken on the microscope.
Create a maximum projection image from the z-stacks, overlaying GFP and mCherry fluorescence.
Use DIC images to ensure analysis of cells in a monolayer.
Scan 10 fields per well of the 96-well plates.
Count the number of cells that have remained in meiosis.
Count the number of cells that have formed buds.
